title: Introspection client interactions emit one structured audit event per named interaction
description: The introspection client emits exactly one structured audit event per introspect call from the `keycloak.introspection` family (verified on `active: true`, refused on `active: false` or non-2xx). Every event carries fields drawn from the fixed allow-list `family` (`keycloak.introspection`), `outcome`, `reasonClass?`, `realmSlug`, `at`. No event may carry a token value (access token, id token, refresh token, introspection response body), a client secret, a raw claim record, or a substring of any of the above. The audit sink is the same one REQ-015 names; sink-failure posture is inherited verbatim (a sink failure logs a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event and never masks the underlying refusal).
rationale: A single cross-cutting audit REQ pointing at one TAC hides ownership when the delivery is spread across TACs. Each TAC that emits an audit family owns its own REQ so a reviewer can see the ownership at a glance and so a future author changing an audit family finds the single REQ that governs it.
